$comment: VAPP-85: the ONE declarative macro table. A macro component (core.catalog.json `kind: macro`) expands into this template before painting; the TS reference expander (src/macros.ts) and the Rust core apply the same table and fixtures/catalog-macros.json locks the output. Template node = { part, component, props?, style?, children?, slots?, $if?, $any?, $each?, $as?, $on?, $context?, $set?, $recipe?, $a11y? }. Values: `"{props.x}"` alone = the raw prop (a data BINDING passes through untouched, so two-way binding survives); `"{props.x|fallback}"` = with a default; `{…}` inside a longer string interpolates; `{id}` = the macro node's id; `{len(props.rows)}` = an array length; `{range(props.max|5)}` = the indexes 0..n-1 (for `$each`); `{index}` = the current $each index; `{!path}` negates. Value objects: $map {from, cases, default}, $cond [condition, then, else], $eq [a, b] (a number equals a string spelling it), $lt [a, b], $add [a, b], $sub [a, b], $clamp [value, min, max] (a missing bound does not clamp), $percent [value, max] (→ "N%"), $coalesce [a, b, …], $text value (→ the value as a string, absent when missing), $not condition, $fill [template, {name: value}] (ALWAYS emits the core `fill` call: the template is usually a `$string.<id>` sentence with `{name}` placeholders the surface's string table resolves at bind time). Object KEYS interpolate too (`"@media (max-width: $breakpoint.{props.collapseBelow|md})"`). `$if` = a condition or an array of conditions (all must hold); `$any` = an array where one must hold. `$each` repeats a part per item of an array (`$as` names the item, default `item`). Children: `"$children"` splices the author's children, `"$slot:name"` splices an author slot in place; `slots: {"trigger": "$slot:trigger"}` copies an author slot, `slots: {"footer": {template node}}` builds one as a part. `$on: {"press": "change"}` routes the author's `on.change` handler to this part's `press` (merging `$context` into an event action's context); without `$on` the author's `on` map stays on the root. `$set: {"press": {"prop": "open", "value": "{!props.open}"}}` = TWO-WAY BINDING (round 1): when the author's `props.open` is a data binding `{path}`, this part's `press` action also carries `functionCall: {call: "set", args: {path, value}}` (the value evaluated like any template value, so usually a call), key order `event` then `functionCall`; a literal prop adds nothing (the host owns the state through the routed event); when the author's routed handler is itself a FUNCTION (an Action carries one), it wins, no `set` is added and the reducer reports an issue. `$a11y: {role, label, description, level, expanded, current, selected, pressed, checked, valueNow, valueMin, valueMax, hidden, autoFocus}` = the part's ACCESSIBILITY (docs/round-1-contract.md §6): evaluated like props (a bound input emits a call) into the expanded node's `accessibility`; `role` is one of catalog/a11y.json `roles`; on the root the author's `accessibility` label/description win. Ids: the root keeps the author's id, parts get `<id>.<part>` and `<id>.<part>.<index>` under `$each`. Every expanded node carries `recipe: {macro, part, props}` where props = `recipeProps` evaluated from the author's props (+ a part's `$recipe`); the THEME (VAPP-92) keys its visual recipes on that, so nothing here states a colour, a border or a font — only structure and token-named spacing, radius and control heights. VAPP-163: the expansion ROOT's recipe also carries `authored` = the top-level keys of the style written ON the macro node (condition blocks count as one key), SORTED, omitted when none; painters apply native recipe < node style < part recipe < those authored keys, so an author's colour or size on a Heading/Badge beats the theme's part recipe while the template's own structure does not (only the author's keys count: a macro node an outer template drew passes on just its root's `authored`, never template style). Macros may use other macros (Row → TreeGuides); expansion recurses until every node is native (innermost recipe wins). ROUND 1 (docs/round-1-contract.md §1, BOUND INPUTS): when an expression input is a data binding `{path}` or a function call, the expander does NOT evaluate — it EMITS an A2UI function call the renderer evaluates at bind time, over the core functions: interpolation → concat, `|fallback` → fallback (as an operand; a whole-string MEMBER of props/style/context passes the binding itself through, so two-way binding survives), `!` → not, len → len, $map → map, $cond → cond, $eq → eq, $lt → lt, $add → add, $sub → sub, $percent → percent, $text → text, $coalesce → coalesce, $not → not; a `$if`/`$any` whose conditions are bound emits the part WITH `visible` = the bound condition (`and{values}` over several bound `$if`s, `or{values}` over several bound `$any`s; literal conditions still decide at expansion); `$each` over a bound array emits nothing (use List with a template); a `$recipe` value may therefore be a call too (renderers resolve recipe props like props). RESPONSIVE PROPS: an author prop `{base, sm?, md?, lg?, xl?}` on a `responsive` prop is evaluated per breakpoint: a part's style is computed with the `base` values, then once per breakpoint named (ascending sm<md<lg<xl, each key inheriting the last smaller one) and every key that changed lands in a `"@media (min-width: $breakpoint.<bp>)"` block of that part; props and conditions see the `base` value. Strings of the form `$string.<id>` (catalog/strings.json) are built-in UI copy the renderer shows in the surface locale. Round 3 (VAPP-102): AFTER the table is applied the core runs ONE post-expansion pass, src/tree-guides.ts applyTreeGuides (Rust: tree_guides::apply): over every node's children in order, each Row root (`recipe.macro` Row, part root) contributes its numeric `recipe.props.depth` (anything else counts as depth 0 and ends every subtree), the ×4 treeGuides rule (elbow at depth-1, tee while a later sibling follows, pass-through for every ancestor level that continues) fills the Row's `guides` part (a TreeGuides) with `elbowAt`/`tee`/`passThrough`; fixtures/tree-guides.json locks the rule, catalog-macros.json the filled trees. EXP-1495 (docs/round-6-contract.md): Outline (the anchor list) and Mosaic (the wide picture group) are macros over Box/Text/Image.
